paragraphs.text: A loose [red tea](red:definition) from Yuchi, in Nantou County, made in 1980. Yuchi lies near Sun Moon Lake, and it is where [Taiwan’s red tea began](red:history), in the Japanese period. This leaf was made the [orthodox](red:whole-and-broken) way: whole strips rolled with care rather than cut or crushed.

At forty-six years it sits well outside the habits of its style. [Red tea has no tradition of ageing](red:ageing): it is made to be drunk fresh, and sealed it is expected to hold for a year and a half to three years. This one has been kept for more than four decades past that span.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
